packageRules.description: A release is proposed only once it is three days old: a compromised or broken release of a tool that runs in CI with the repository token (or that builds what is published: setuptools, build, twine) is usually yanked or fixed within that time. Every pin is a release with a date: requirements-lint.txt / requirements-test.txt / requirements-build.txt, the build back end in pyproject.toml, the actions' version tags, the hook repositories' revisions in .pre-commit-config.yaml (github-tags, see the pre-commit rule below). Digest-only updates are left out: the hassfest action and the HACS validation image follow a branch or a moving tag, where there is no release to age, and holding them would only keep the validators stale.

pytest-homeassistant-custom-component pins homeassistant, pytest, pytest-asyncio, pytest-cov, pytest-timeout and syrupy to exact versions, so requirements-test.txt pins only it: the whole test stack moves with it, in one PR, and Renovate never proposes a Home Assistant or pytest release it does not support yet. The ci.yml `library` job reads its test-runner pins from the same release's metadata and its mypy and hypothesis from requirements-test.txt (hypothesis is pinned there on its own: the Home Assistant test stack does not pin it). The packaging tools are pinned in requirements-build.txt and the build back end in pyproject.toml `[build-system]` (Renovate's pip_requirements and pep621 managers read both by themselves); the `usb` integration's requirements are not pinned anywhere: ci.yml reads them from the installed Home Assistant's manifest, so they follow HA's pins by construction. This rule only names the update so it is recognisable in the PR list.

The HACS validation image (ci.yml runs ghcr.io/hacs/action:main by digest, not through the hacs/action wrapper): `docker:pinDigests` above keeps the digest moving along the `main` tag; this rule only names the update so it is recognisable in the PR list.

The workflow linters of the ci.yml `lint` job (actionlint, whose image carries shellcheck, and zizmor) run as images by tag and digest: `docker:pinDigests` above keeps the digest moving with the tag. Both only read the checkout, without the repository token, and a new release can only make `lint` stricter, so they move together in one PR, named so it is recognisable. The ci.yml `library` job pins no Python version for Renovate to move: it reads the oldest one from pyproject.toml `requires-python`, so the floor the package promises is the one it is tested on.

The hooks of .pre-commit-config.yaml (ruff-pre-commit, pre-commit-hooks) are pinned to a commit with the tag it carries (`rev: <sha>  # frozen: vX`, as `pre-commit autoupdate --freeze` writes them). Renovate's pre-commit manager is off by default; `:enablePreCommit` above turns it on, and it moves both the commit and the tag in the comment. The tags come from the github-tags datasource, so the three-day rule above holds them like every other pin. The `local` hooks (the privacy scan, mypy) run the repository's own code and have no revision. This rule only names the update so it is recognisable in the PR list.

ruff is pinned twice: in requirements-lint.txt (CI's `lint` job, `nox -s lint`) and as the ruff-pre-commit hook revision, which carries the same version. One PR moves both, so a commit hook never checks with another ruff than CI. The group takes precedence over the pre-commit hooks group above for ruff (a later rule wins).
